adoption.notes: The runtime signs the unchanged command bytes and never reissues a command: egress publishes once, held by tests on its call sites, its scheduling and its client. It reads rate_limited only as a firmware-telemetry/v2 fault. It drives no firmware-commanded zone, so the Tier D attempt carve-out has no runtime path yet. No conformance claim is made, so the version is not frozen by this merge. From 02b33b1d it signs commands and liveness in the domains of Signing Domains, and only for a device whose manifest declares runtime_key_domains; for any other device it signs nothing and reports its runtime_commanded actions unavailable. From a39d551b it can draw each liveness nonce from a secure source and keep the liveness table, but does both, and publishes liveness at v 2, only while gateway.firmware_commands.publish_liveness_v2 is on, and it is off by default. Off, it publishes liveness at v 1 alone; on, it publishes a v 1 and v 2 pair. Neither is what Which v the runtime publishes requires, liveness at v 2 alone. No released runtime does any of this: v2.5.0 signs commands and liveness over the object bytes alone.

Its device verifier implements runtime liveness at v 1, which firmware-commands/v1's baseline audit moved to this version's Runtime Liveness section, and records whether the runtime is reachable as shadow observability only: no Local Interlock is gated on it. It signs the rate_limited verdict at fault v 2 from a3c54c2. From a2c528f it verifies commands and liveness only in the domains of Signing Domains, and every manifest it signs declares runtime_key_domains. From ee35e34 it accepts liveness at v 1 and at v 2 with one high-water mark, holds the nonce of the last accepted v 2 message in memory, clears it on an accepted v 1 message, a manifest or runtime key change, expiry and boot, and takes liveness through its own inbound lane, apart from commands and provisioning. Its builds from a2c528f until ee35e34 carry runtime_key_domains without accepting liveness at v 2, which Which v the runtime publishes does not permit; none was released. Its DECISIONS.md D-047, core/signer.h and core/manifest.c still describe the declaration as the domains alone, no firmware test ties the declaration to accepting liveness at v 2, and D-048 still expects a v 1 and v 2 pair per interval. Its mirror of liveness-vectors-v2.json is byte-identical to this repository's. It signs no envelope at v 2 and no liveness_nonce, so nothing it signs carries the held nonce yet. No conformance claim is made, and the evidence is host tests, not a device or HIL.

notes: Exists for the rate_limited verdict, which answers relay_close only, and for the rule that a runtime never reissues a command to recover its delivery. Fresh open_protected_circuit attempts for a latched Tier D trip are not reissues and continue, under the binding the governing safety-profile contract authorizes. Command and provisioning approval bytes are v1's and keep v 1. Runtime liveness at v 1 keeps the grammar of this version's Runtime Liveness section and gains v 2, carrying a fresh 128-bit nonce from which the signing runtime bounds how long ago a device began the transaction behind a reading, under firmware-telemetry/v2. A device that declares runtime_key_domains accepts liveness at v 2, and the runtime publishes liveness to it at v 2 alone, never at v 1. The edge firmware accepts liveness at v 2 and carries runtime_key_domains; the runtime implements the nonce and the liveness table, but publishes v 2 only behind a flag that is off by default. That is implementation, not end-to-end or HIL proof, and no device image gates a Local Interlock on liveness. The runtime has adopted the rate_limited and no-reissue rules; the edge firmware signs the rate_limited verdict from a3c54c2. The runtime adopts it before any device signs a v 2 fault, and devices accept liveness v 2 before the runtime publishes it. The runtime command key signs a command and a liveness message only in the domain of its purpose, under Signing Domains, keeps no v 1 form, and signs for a device only while its manifest declares runtime_key_domains under firmware-telemetry/v2. Both implementations sign or verify in those domains on their main branches, and no release of either does.
